text:
sara (support): @oliver @raj ACME reporting ~30m of 503s on hosted inference. They see timeouts and 500s on generate endpoints. Ticket #12345, customer on a call asking for ETA. :rotating_light:

morgan (cs): they're seeing repeated billing hits too — wants errors paused or credit while we investigate.

oliver (oncall): grabbing logs now. Gateway shows 502->503 surge starting 2024-11-03T16:12:08Z. K8s events: multiple infer-runner pods OOMKilled and Restarting. Model pinned: redwood-7b-q4.

raj (eng-runtime): can you paste the container logs + exact model/config? We deployed a quant-swap change yesterday that touched prefetch code.

ci-bot: metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runner/infer-pods?panel=Errors - p95 latency spike, restart_count spike for deployment/redwood-7b-q4-runner

sara (support): paste of most recent runner log snippet:
```
[2024-11-03 16:11:59] infer-runner[pid=2143]: starting prefetch context ctx=abcd
[2024-11-03 16:12:02] infer-runtime: KV prefetch size=1.1G tokens=4096
[2024-11-03 16:12:02] CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 1228800000 bytes
[2024-11-03 16:12:02] infer-runner[pid=2143]: uncaught signal: Segmentation fault (signal 11)
[2024-11-03 16:12:03] kubelet: Killing container with id docker://infer-runner sha: OOMKilled
restart_count: 4
```

lee (eng-sre): quick check: dmesg on node shows oom-killer target=2143 and nv-peer-reset events for GPU0 around the same time. That indicates kernel-level GPU reset triggered by the process, not just container cgroup mem. Node free GPU memory before event ~1.2GB.

raj (eng-runtime): this matches a regression we saw in the prefetch path: if prefetch tries to materialize a large KV block when context=4096 and batchsize>=12 on q4 quantization, we can try to allocate >1GB and race with other shards -> CUDA OOM then segfault on the next mem access. Repro steps I can run locally:
```bash
# repro (synthetic)
./infer_local --model redwood-7b-q4 --context 4096 --batch 16 --prefetch on --tokens 2000 --seed 42
```
I can reproduce an OOM in ~12-15s on a GPU with other small services running.

oliver (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) apply immediate soft-limit in hosted routing to route new requests for redwood-7b-q4 -> redwood-7b-q2-small for accounts hitting >3 restarts, 2) reduce max_batch_size from 16->6 for the hot deployment, 3) disable quant-swap for ACME specifically. I'll start a canary rollout of the batch cap now.

morgan (cs): told customer we'll apply fallbacks and request billing hold for the affected window. They're amenable to temporary model fallback if errors stop. :white_check_mark:

raj (eng-runtime): I'll push a hotfix to runtime that adds a guard: if free_gpu_mem < 1.5G then cap requested prefetch allocation and refuse batches larger than 8. Preparing a PR (link forthcoming). Also adding better OOM handling to avoid segfault after CUDA failure.

lee (eng-sre): created a short-running probe to watch restart_count on infer-runner and auto-route when >3 within 10m. Patch applied to canary.

ci-bot: deploy: runtime-hotfix/2024-11-03-oom-guard -> canary (2 pods) started at 2024-11-03T16:22:10Z

raj (eng-runtime): hotfix deployed to canary, running repro against canary now. If green will roll to prod in 10m.

oliver (oncall): after canary we saw restart_count stop increasing for canary pods; gateway error rate for ACME drop from 14% -> 1.8% over 6m. Rolling to prod now.

sara (support): ACME confirmed errors largely stopped after fallback + rollback, they requested postmortem + root cause. I'll keep ticket updated and schedule follow-up with CS+Eng. :eyes:

morgan (cs): opening billing case for credit.

raj (eng-runtime): root cause notes for postmortem: regression in KV prefetch allocation path interacting with q4 quantization and high batch sizes -> allocation spike -> CUDA OOM -> runtime did not gracefully handle CUDA failure leading to segfault and container restart. Fix: prefetch guards, OOM-safe path, and autoscaler routing.

lee (eng-sre): will add node-level alert for nvml reset spikes + restart_count anomaly rule to catch this earlier.

sara (support): thanks all — updating ticket #12345 with mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem doc.
